_comment: song.json skeleton — fill this in and then run scripts/generate.py (or make_datapack.py). For the field reference see references/format_spec.md §B; keys starting with an underscore are comments and are ignored.

meta.name: mysong
meta._name: song name (lowercase ASCII, used for paths and file names)
meta._namespace: datapack namespace; minecraft is the simplest, but you can also use your own name
meta._path: function path → /function <namespace>:<path>/play. The community convention is music/<song name>
meta._song_id: song selection id for music_type. Inside a lemon-family host it must not collide with an existing song (the original lemon pack occupies 8)
meta._mc_version: target MC version: decides the instrument whitelist and the pack.mcmeta syntax. pling/bit/banjo need 1.14+, trumpet needs 26.1+
meta._style: standalone = ships its own init/tick tags and installs on its own; lemon = emits only the song folder to hang off an existing host
meta._time_unit: with nbs_s_units, t is the game tick (1/20 second) — the only timeline convention that has been measured, recommended
meta._speed: the value of #speed nbs_s. The host adds this much to nbs_s every tick, and the tree window is 80×t; t equals the game tick only at 80
meta._auto_stop: true = automatically chain into stop on the last note tick
meta._mute_tag: players carrying this tag cannot hear this song

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: lead melody track: 1 track holds 1 part, which makes it easy to include/exclude a whole track on user request

notes._comment: t = note onset (the game tick under this convention, 1 = 0.05s); midi = pitch; vol may be omitted and defaults to 1.0; inst can override this track's default instrument
several notes on the same tick with the same instrument = a chord, kept in full (dedup only by tick+instrument+pitch)
accompaniment/chords default to volume 1.0; notes outside the pitch range are folded by an octave at generation time with a warning
the bass base is F#1(30), reaching 30..54; lower notes must be raised an octave
the drum midi is arbitrary (using 54 = use-count 12 = pitch 1.0); always keep volumes on the quiet side
